data.name: Athman
data.gender_notes: Athman is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Sanskrit word 'Athman' is derived from 'Atma', meaning self, soul or breath. In Hinduism, 'Athman' is considered the eternal, individual soul, and is the essence of all living beings. The name Athman carries the meaning “Breath, Soul” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Athman usually hope their child will grow to embody breath, soul and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of the immortal soul and connection to the divine.
data.etymology: Athman belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Breath, Soul.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Athman total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Athman' holds deep cultural significance for Hindus, as it signifies the concept of the individual self, which is believed to be a part of the universal consciousness. This concept is ingrained in various aspects of Indian art, literature, and philosophy. For instance, the Upanishads, which are ancient Hindu scriptures, contain numerous teachings on the 'Athman', imparting wisdom about self-realization, eternal life, and the ultimate truth of the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Athman' embodies the deep-rooted belief in the existence of the eternal soul, or self, which transcends the physical body. The Hindu tradition holds that every individual has an 'Athman', which acts as the controlling force, the essence of consciousness, and the highest expression of an individual's spiritual identity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Athman is a Sanskrit word meaning 'the eternal self or soul'. It symbolizes the innermost essence of an individual, the divine spark within each being. It is the deep, unchanging core of consciousness that transcends the physical body and connects us all to the Universe.

historical_references.reference: The Upanishads, a collection of texts on Indian philosophy, discuss the concept of Atman or the self. These texts date back to around 800-500 BCE and were composed in various Indian languages.
